title: briqyard: host
description: One host: machines, capacity, pool, disks, network, boots, warm reservations and host preparation/readiness.

panels.title: State
panels.description: The host's state in the fleet's registry.

panels.title: Answering
panels.description: Whether the fleet relayed the host's metrics at the last scrape.

panels.title: Machines
panels.description: Machines on the host, gateways included.

panels.title: Running
panels.description: Machines running now.

panels.title: Namespaces
panels.description: Namespaces with a machine or a gateway here.

panels.title: Endpoints
panels.description: Ports of its machines served by its ingress.

panels.title: Conditions
panels.description: The host's conditions over time, red while true: memory_pressure (committed memory over 95 % of capacity), disk_pressure (the pool under 10 % free) and any other it reports.

panels.title: Machines by state
panels.description: Every machine on the host by its state now; error in red.

panels.title: Stopped, by why
panels.description: Stopped machines: idle (asleep, the next use wakes them), user (asked), exit (their process ended), host (the host stopped them; they wake as asleep ones do).

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: What the host hands out to machines, what running machines reserved, and what their processes hold (cgroups).

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: vCPUs the host hands out, vCPUs of running machines, and the cores their processes use.

panels.title: Committed
panels.description: Memory committed over capacity. memory_pressure at 95 %.

panels.title: Pool used
panels.description: The pool's used space over its size. disk_pressure under 10 % free.

panels.title: Pool
panels.description: The pool's used and free space (its datasets, snapshots and memory snapshots).

panels.title: Disk used by machines
panels.description: What the machines' disks, their snapshots and memory snapshots take on the pool: the five namespaces that take the most.

panels.title: Disk throughput
panels.description: Bytes the guests read from and wrote to their disks (Firecracker's metrics, a line a minute). Writes below the axis.

panels.title: Network
panels.description: Internet traffic through the host's NAT and endpoint traffic through its ingress. Outbound below the axis.

panels.title: Held back by limits
panels.description: Disk requests the disk limits held back, and packets the egress limits dropped.

panels.title: Boot time
panels.description: Each machine's last start, starting to running (a resume included): the median and the 95th percentile across the host's machines.

panels.title: Starts
panels.description: Cold boots, resumes from a memory snapshot, stops with one, and starts that failed, per interval.

panels.title: Restarts
panels.description: Restarts by the machines' restart policy, and crash loops (the third restart in ten minutes and each after), per interval.

panels.title: Events by reason
panels.description: Every event the host logged, per interval, by reason.

panels.title: Commands and backups
panels.description: Commands run in machines (exec sessions included) and backups sent to the store, per interval.

panels.title: Warm pools: host preparation and reservations
Warm slots on this host
panels.description: Actual pool records and upper targets. Ready means a paused host slot; it does not measure public API readiness.

panels.title: Warm slots by pool, type and exact size
panels.description: Each configured pool, its desired target and paused-ready shortfall. Claim transfers ownership; it does not return a machine to the pool.

panels.title: Warm RAM reservations
panels.description: Full recipe RAM, including creating and unreleased slots. Reservations are distinct from resident use. Headroom applies at warm admission; ordinary workloads may consume it later.

panels.title: Warm CPU reservations (millis)
panels.description: Full CPU-time reservations against operator budget and ordinary-workload admission headroom.

panels.title: Warm logical root reservations
panels.description: Full logical root sizes, including failed or unreleased slots. These are not physical disk usage; copy-on-write sharing does not reduce the reservation.

panels.title: Measured available RAM and floor
panels.description: Cached MemAvailable and configured physical floor. Admission additionally subtracts conservative fill liabilities. See probe age and validity before interpreting this measurement.

panels.title: Physical pool free space and floor
panels.description: Cached physical free space and the configured absolute floor. Admission also preserves the existing percentage floor and full logical root liabilities.

panels.title: Warm probe age
panels.description: Age of the cached availability sample. The admission age bound is five seconds. Scrapes do not run probes; no sample is displayed until one exists.

panels.title: Warm admission observations
panels.description: Actual unfinished fills, configured maximum, cached-probe presence/age validity and accounting availability. Values of one indicate available or valid observations.

panels.title: Blocked warm pools
panels.description: Last persisted blockage by a bounded reason. Cleanup blockage remains visible for draining, unreleased slots; raw errors are not metric labels.

panels.title: Blocked refill attempts
panels.description: Actual refused refill attempts per interval. A target is an upper bound and may remain unfilled while resources or headroom are unavailable.

panels.title: Warm host preparation and claim readiness (mean)
panels.description: Mean successful prepare-worker duration and claim-to-host-readiness duration. Excludes fleet and public API transport. No duration appears until routine operations have been observed.

panels.title: Warm misses and failures
panels.description: Host claim misses, including empty or busy pools, and host prepare/claim failures per interval. This does not measure public API end-to-end latency.

panels.title: Unique machines observed running
panels.description: Distinct machine identities observed running in the selected period, gateways included. Requires a running scrape: starts and stops entirely between scrapes may be missed. Not a count of machines first created in this period. Zero is shown only when at least one successful scrape of this host was observed in the selected period; otherwise the panel has no data.

targets.expr: count(max by (machine) (max_over_time(briqyard_machine_state{state="running", host="$host"}[$__range])) == 1) or (vector(0) and on() (max(max_over_time(up{job="briqyard", host="$host"}[$__range])) == 1))

panels.title: Successful starts and resumes
panels.description: Successful start and resume events in the selected period, including restarts and wakes. Event count, not unique machines; counter increases are estimated between scrapes. Zero is shown only when at least one successful scrape of this host was observed in the selected period; otherwise the panel has no data.

targets.expr: sum(increase(briqyard_events_total{type="normal", reason=~"started|resumed", host="$host"}[$__range])) or (vector(0) and on() (max(max_over_time(up{job="briqyard", host="$host"}[$__range])) == 1))
